one_month_reasoning: Inside the window: Q3 2026 earnings ~Oct 22 (guided Q3 sales 750 Mlb Cu, 160 koz Au; Grasberg ~65% of capacity in H2; realized copper ~$6.3-6.7/lb vs $6.00 guidance assumption, so a beat on price is likely already priced; the swing factor is any change to the Grasberg ramp schedule, which has been the stock's main idiosyncratic driver in 2026). Also possible any day: White House decision on the Section 232 refined-copper tariff (15% from Jan-2027 recommended; SocGen reads ~15% odds for 2027), the Escondida strike outcome, and LME stock rebuilds that have cooled rallies quickly. Short-horizon regularities: stock is ~12% off its August high after a +98% year, copper at records; momentum and reversal roughly offset. I stay near-symmetric: median ~$70.3 (slight drag from mean-reversion after record copper), monthly sigma 14% (48%/3.5 plus a small earnings premium).

fair_value.method: Blend of 2027E EV/EBITDA (EBITDA $13.5B at $5.50/lb copper x 8.5x, less NCI ~18% of EV and $5.3B net debt incl. downstream) = $61 and 2027E P/E ($2.80 EPS x 22x) = $62; weighted 60/40 -> ~$62.

bear.story: Copper mean-reverts toward $4.75-5.00/lb as tariff-pull inventories unwind and China slows; sector multiples compress from 12x to ~8x; any further Grasberg slippage. Matches the historical pattern: FCX was down 20-75% 12 months after the 2008, 2011, 2021 and 2024 copper records.

base.story: Copper eases to ~$5.50-6.00, Grasberg reaches ~80% by mid-2027 and near-full by year-end, volume growth offsets price; multiple drifts to FCX's historical 8-9x EBITDA.

bull.story: Supply deficit persists (Grasberg/Kamoa outages, tariffs), copper $7-10/lb per Deutsche Bank's scramble thesis; Grasberg back to full, FCX re-rates toward peer multiples.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$45 (~-36%) the market would be pricing copper under ~$4.75/lb or a structural Grasberg problem (further ramp delay, Indonesian regime/licence issue); that is beyond ordinary 48%-vol noise within a year and would mean the supply-deficit thesis failed.

reasoning: Base rates first: from 20 years of FCX monthly closes, unconditional 12m forward return median is ~-1% with log-sd ~0.54 (10th/90th pct -45%/+84%); conditional on a trailing +60% year the median is +22% but that sample is dominated by early-recovery rallies (2009-10, 2016-17, 2020-21). The better analogue is copper at an all-time record: after the 2008, Feb-2011, May-2021 and May-2024 records FCX was lower 12 months later in every case (-75%, -20%, -9%, -27%). Today copper is at records ($6.8/lb) on supply shocks and tariff stockpiling, sector EV/EBITDA ~12x vs ~8x long-run, yet FCX itself only prices ~$5.90/lb copper and has idiosyncratic volume growth as Grasberg ramps (65% -> 80% mid-2027 -> near-full end-2027), which differentiates it from prior peaks. Fair value ~$62 at $5.50/lb and 8.5x/22x; consensus target ~$70, Bernstein $47, MS $66. Macro: Kalshi prices a 2026 recession at ~5% (Aug), so the downside is more copper-specific than macro. I set the median at ~$66 (-6%), mixing lognormals with sigma 0.42/0.52 for fat tails consistent with 48% realized vol, giving P(>=71) ~0.44. Research limited to ~12 queries; analyst-estimate API data was unavailable.
